Script.name: group
Script.script: --[[ Group Panel — the party, in a window you can move Sean Stoves, 2026-08-02 One row per member, straight off gmcp.group: a health bar with the member written across it, mana and moves as thin bars under it, and alignment as a strip along the bottom. [ *201 Solao 3 1204 ] <- level, name, quests today, tnl [ ====================== ] <- mana [ ====================== ] <- moves [ ---------------------- ] <- align, coloured by which way it leans The layout and the field order are the stock module's. What's different: Theirs is nailed under the minimap, and each member's container is parented to the one above it - a chain fifty deep, so row 9 is a great-great-grandchild of row 1. This is a panel like every other one here: drag it, resize it, dock it, and the rows resize to fit whatever height you give it. Theirs builds an alignment bar for every member and calls hide() on it twice, once at creation and once per update, so nobody has ever seen it. The data was always in GMCP. Here it's the strip along the bottom, and the colour is the point: green leaning good, red leaning evil, grey near neutral. Theirs also has `if not (gmcp.char.maxstats) then return end` in the middle of the member loop. That's a return from the whole function rather than the iteration, so before your own maxstats arrive - the first seconds after connect - every member after you in the list stops being drawn. Not carried across: their damage-share bar. It needs a combat trigger reading the bracketed damage numbers, which are off unless you've turned them on, and it seeds every member with a free point of damage so the percentages are fiction until the first real hit lands. Same call as the potion count in Gauges - a number that's usually wrong is worse than no number. 'group' is the MUD's command and stays the MUD's. This one is 'grouppanel'. ]] aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.group = aardkit.group or {} local GR = aardkit.group local U = aardkit.util.named("Group Panel") local G = aardkit.gmcp local CFG = U.load("group", { on = true, align = true, -- ON. Installing this takes the group display over, through their own -- aard.config["group"] switch rather than by disabling a script by name. -- A switch, not a one-way door - 'grouppanel standalone off' hands it back. standalone = true, }) local function save() U.save("group", CFG) end --- -- their colours, same as the Gauges module reads them out of their config --- local COL = { health = { "#1aa41a", "#005500" }, mana = { "#4570fc", "#1133cc" }, moves = { "#b0b051", "#555511" }, good = { "#d98839", "#814100" }, neutral = { "#888888", "#444444" }, evil = { "#8c2929", "#410000" }, } local BACK = "#101418" local LEADER = "#e0ffff" -- their proportions: a fat bar for health, thin ones for the rest local ROW_MAX, ROW_MIN = 26, 14 -- Declared above every function that reads them. A local read from a function -- written earlier in the file is a nil global - this project did that nine -- times before there was a gate for it, and three of those shipped. local rows = {} -- member index -> { hp = gauge, mn = ..., mv = ..., al = ... } local unframed = false local function front(c1, c2) return "background-color: QLinearGradient(x1:0, y1:0, x2:0, y2:1," .. " stop:0 " .. c1 .. ", stop:1 " .. c2 .. ");" end -- Gauge text is HTML, so real spaces collapse and columns drift apart. local function pad(s, n, right) s = tostring(s or "") if #s > n then s = s:sub(1, n) end local fill = string.rep(" ", n - #s) return right and (fill .. s) or (s .. fill) end --- -- what GMCP gives us -- -- Field names are theirs, out of their onGroup - name, and info.{lvl,tnl,qt, -- hp,mhp,mn,mmn,mv,mmv,align,here}. Every read is nil-safe: a member who has -- just joined can arrive with info missing entirely. --- function GR.members() local g = G.val("group") if type(g) ~= "table" or type(g.members) ~= "table" then return {}, nil end return g.members, g.leader end --- -- the panel --- local panel = aardkit.panel.new({ -- "grouppanel", not "group": their containers are group1..group50 and -- their table of them is a global called group. Nothing of ours needs to -- sit that close to it. name = "grouppanel", title = "Group", x = "1050px", y = "40px", width = 320, height = 160, consoleless = true, onbuild = function() rows = {} if aardkit.group and aardkit.group.paint then aardkit.group.paint() end end, onresize = function() if aardkit.group and aardkit.group.paint then aardkit.group.paint() end end, }) GR.panel = panel local function make_row(i) local gen = panel.gen or 1 local function gauge(part) local ok, b = pcall(function() return Geyser.Gauge:new({ name = "aardkit_group_" .. part .. "_" .. i .. "_" .. gen, x = 0, y = 0, width = 10, height = 10, }, panel.container) end) return ok and b or nil end local r = { hp = gauge("hp"), mn = gauge("mn"), mv = gauge("mv"), al = gauge("al") } if not r.hp then return nil end for key, part in pairs({ hp = "health", mn = "mana", mv = "moves", al = "neutral" }) do local b = r[key] if b then pcall(function() b.back:setStyleSheet("background-color: " .. BACK .. ";") end) local c = COL[part] pcall(function() b.front:setStyleSheet(front(c[1], c[2])) end) end end return r end -- Rows shrink to fit the height you gave the panel rather than spilling out of -- the bottom of it, which is the whole reason this is a panel and not a strip -- welded under the minimap. function GR.layout(count) if not panel.container then return end local w = U.px(panel.container.get_width and panel.container:get_width() or panel.container.width) local h = U.px(panel.container.get_height and panel.container:get_height() or panel.container.height) if w < 40 or h < 20 or count < 1 then return end local rh = math.floor(h / count) if rh > ROW_MAX then rh = ROW_MAX end if rh < ROW_MIN then rh = ROW_MIN end -- health takes what's left after the thin ones, so a squeezed row loses the -- big bar's height rather than dropping the small bars off the bottom local thin = math.max(2, math.floor((rh - 2) / 6)) local align = CFG.align and thin or 0 local fat = rh - (thin * 2) - align - 2 -- One owner for what is on screen, and it is this loop. A second pass in -- update() hid departed rows as well, which meant a control aimed at either -- one passed on the strength of the other - the coverage read as real and -- wasn't. Widgets are kept rather than destroyed so the next join is instant. for i, r in pairs(rows) do local y = (i - 1) * rh if i > count or fat < 4 then for _, b in pairs(r) do pcall(function() b:hide() end) end else local function place(b, top, height) if not b then return end pcall(function() b:show() end) pcall(function() b:move(0, top) end) pcall(function() b:resize(w, height) end) end place(r.hp, y, fat) place(r.mn, y + fat, thin) place(r.mv, y + fat + thin, thin) if CFG.align then place(r.al, y + fat + thin * 2, align) elseif r.al then pcall(function() r.al:hide() end) end end end end function GR.paint() if not panel.container then return end local members = GR.members() local count = #members for i = 1, count do if not rows[i] then rows[i] = make_row(i) end end GR.layout(count) GR.update() end --- -- filling them in --- -- Group alignment runs to 2500, not the 1000 a character's own align uses - -- the wiki's own example payload has "align": 2500, and their group bar scales -- to 2500 with its bands at +/-875. I had it on a 1000 scale with +/-350 bands, -- which pegged anything over 1000 at full and coloured the middle wrongly. local ALIGN_MAX = 2500 local function band(al) if al >= 875 then return "good" end if al <= -875 then return "evil" end return "neutral" end function GR.update() if not CFG.on or not panel.container then return end local members, leader = GR.members() local count = #members if count == 0 then for _, r in pairs(rows) do for _, b in pairs(r) do pcall(function() b:hide() end) end end return end -- a member joining or leaving changes how many rows we need local have = 0 for i in pairs(rows) do if i > have then have = i end end if have < count then GR.paint(); return end for i = 1, count do local m = members[i] or {} local r = rows[i] local info = type(m.info) == "table" and m.info or {} if r and r.hp then local name = tostring(m.name or "?") local hp, mhp = tonumber(info.hp) or 0, math.max(1, tonumber(info.mhp) or 1) local mn, mmn = tonumber(info.mn) or 0, math.max(1, tonumber(info.mmn) or 1) local mv, mmv = tonumber(info.mv) or 0, math.max(1, tonumber(info.mmv) or 1) -- 'here' is 0 when they're somewhere else, which is the one thing -- you want to see at a glance when the tank stops taking damage local mark = (tonumber(info.here) == 0) and "*" or " " local shown = (name == leader) and ('' .. pad(name, 12) .. "") or pad(name, 12) local text = "" .. mark .. pad(info.lvl or "?", 3, true) .. " " .. shown .. " " .. pad(info.qt or "", 2, true) .. " " .. pad(info.tnl or "", 5, true) .. "" pcall(function() r.hp:setValue(math.min(hp, mhp), mhp, text) end) if r.mn then pcall(function() r.mn:setValue(math.min(mn, mmn), mmn) end) end if r.mv then pcall(function() r.mv:setValue(math.min(mv, mmv), mmv) end) end if r.al and CFG.align then local al = tonumber(info.align) or 0 local c = COL[band(al)] pcall(function() r.al.front:setStyleSheet(front(c[1], c[2])) end) pcall(function() r.al:setValue(math.abs(al), ALIGN_MAX) end) end end end end --- -- standing theirs down -- -- Their own switch, the same call the mapper makes: aard.config["group"] is -- read at the top of their onGroup - 0 does nothing, 1 draws the panel - so -- setting it to 0 is what their author put there for this. Better than -- disabling onGroup by name, which would survive exactly until they rename it. -- -- Setting it to 0 doesn't retract what's already on screen, because their -- onGroup returns before reaching its own hide loop, so we hide their rows -- ourselves. Going back the other way needs no such help: their next group -- message re-shows every container it owns. -- -- One thing goes quiet with it. Their onGroup is also where aard.group[name] -- gets seeded, which is what their damage and party-heal triggers count into. -- Those triggers check the table before touching it, so nothing breaks - the -- counters just stop, and nothing but their panel ever read them. --- function GR.their_group(on) if type(aard) ~= "table" or type(aard.config) ~= "table" then return false end aard.config["group"] = on and 1 or 0 if not on then local grp = _G.group if type(grp) == "table" then for i = 1, 50 do local w = grp[i] if type(w) ~= "table" then break end pcall(function() w:hide() end) end end local info = _G.gInfo if type(info) == "table" then pcall(function() info:hide() end) end end return true end local function stand_down() if not CFG.standalone or not aard then return end if unframed then return end if GR.their_group(false) then unframed = true U.note("Stock group display stood down via their own aard.config group switch" .. " - 'grouppanel standalone off' hands it back.") end end --- -- commands --- function GR.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg) rest = U.trim(rest) if aardkit.panel.verb("grouppanel", verb, rest) then return end if verb == "" or verb == "help" then local members, leader = GR.members() local g = G.val("group") or {} U.help("Group Panel", { { "state", CFG.on and "on" or "off" }, { "group", #members > 0 and (#members .. " member(s), led by " .. tostring(leader or "?")) or "not in one" }, -- the rest of what the group message carries, which nothing read { "name", tostring(g.groupname or "-") .. " (" .. tostring(g.status or "?") .. ")" }, { "since", tostring(g.created or "-") }, { "kills", tostring(g.kills or 0) .. " exp " .. tostring(g.exp or 0) }, { "align", CFG.align and "shown" or "hidden" }, { "" }, { "grouppanel on|off", "stop updating it" }, { "grouppanel align on|off", "the alignment strip under each member" }, { "grouppanel show|hide|dock|embed", "where the window lives" }, { "grouppanel standalone on|off", "stop the stock module's own group display" }, { "grouppanel opacity <0-255>", "how solid this window is; 'default' follows the shared setting" }, { "" }, { "'group' is the MUD's own command and stays that way - this one" }, { "answers to 'grouppanel'." }, { "" }, { "Their damage-share bar is not carried across: it needs the" }, { "bracketed damage numbers turned on, and it gives everyone a free" }, { "point of damage so the percentages read wrong until the first" }, { "real hit lands." }, }) elseif verb == "on" or verb == "off" then CFG.on = (verb == "on"); save() U.ok("Group panel " .. verb .. ".") if CFG.on then GR.paint() end elseif verb == "align" then CFG.align = (rest:lower() ~= "off"); save() GR.paint() U.ok("Alignment strip " .. (CFG.align and "on" or "off") .. ".") elseif verb == "standalone" then local v = rest:lower() if v ~= "on" and v ~= "off" then U.help("Standalone group panel", { { "state", CFG.standalone and "on - ours has the group" or "off - theirs is drawing it too" }, { "installed", aard and "the stock module is here" or "none, nothing to do" }, { "" }, { "onGroup (their script)", "stood down via aard.config group = 0" }, { "", "-> this panel, which you can move" }, { "" }, { "Their switch, not ours: their onGroup reads that value on its" }, { "first line. It also stops their damage and party-heal counters," }, { "which are seeded in the same place and read by nothing else." }, { "" }, { "grouppanel standalone on|off", "switch it" }, }) return end CFG.standalone = (v == "on"); save() if not aard then U.note("The stock module isn't installed - ours already has the group."); return end if v == "on" then unframed = false stand_down() U.ok("Stock group display down - ours has the group.") else GR.their_group(true) unframed = false U.ok("Stock group display back on - it redraws on the next group message.") end elseif verb == "show" or verb == "hide" or verb == "dock" or verb == "embed" then aardkit.panel.cmd("grouppanel " .. verb .. (rest ~= "" and (" " .. rest) or "")) if verb ~= "hide" then GR.paint() end else U.warn("grouppanel on|off | align on|off | show|hide|dock|embed ('grouppanel help')") end end aardkit.register("grouppanel", "the party, in a window you can move", GR.cmd) -- Every group message: a member's hp changing is exactly what this is for, and -- waiting a tick to show the tank dropping defeats the point. -- Aardwolf sends no group data at all until asked - the one package with its -- own toggle on top of Core.Supports. Declared here because this is what uses it. aardkit.gmcp.need("group", "Group 1", "group on") aardkit.gmcp.watch("group", "group", "aardkit.group.paint", true) GR.paint() -- guiLoad builds their group widgets on connect rather than at script load, so -- the load-time attempts pass before there is anything to stand down. for _, t in ipairs({ 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 }) do tempTimer(t, stand_down) end U.killhandler(aardkit_group_connect) aardkit_group_connect = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysConnectionEvent", function() for _, t in ipairs({ 2, 6, 12, 20 }) do tempTimer(t, stand_down) end end)
